title: Trump insists he's not downplaying AI risk, says there is a 'SICK conspiracy' against data centers
source_used: ABC7 San Francisco (carries an ABC News report)
key_facts: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said his company would welcome a slower pace of AI development so that capabilities do not "get ahead of alignment and monitoring"; he added that "pacing" does not mean "stopping".

Altman said late on Sunday that OpenAI would welcome a federal framework "that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI", but does not believe it needs to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to start the work.
Altman named two dangers to avoid: an "unacceptable" loss of control over AI, and too much concentration of power in one person, company or country.

President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters on Sunday on the way back from Ireland, said he would not downplay AI concerns, that there would be "more good than bad", and that "Whoever wins AI wins".

In a social media post on Monday Trump wrote that the only "guardrails" AI needs is "a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT" and that there is a "SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers" that only China is happy about.

Vice President JD Vance said Monday the administration is "concerned" and that regulation must be done "smartly"; he said it feels "a bit of a Trojan horse" that so many frontier AI companies ask government to regulate them.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on ABC's "This Week" on Sunday that Congress should act urgently and slow the pace of AI development.

Background in the article: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei wrote last week that "we must pace the frontier"; former safety researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic and warned about AI risk; lawmakers return this week for the last push before the November midterms.
quote_evidence: Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, joined others in the artificial intelligence industry in saying that his company would welcome a slower development pace for AI to ensure that the technology's capabilities don't "get ahead of alignment and monitoring," as President Donald Trump said there would be "more good than bad" from the technology.

He added that there is a "SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China," and that the U.S. is "leading China" as well as other countries in the technology.
Altman on Sunday said, "When we talk about 'pacing', we do not mean 'stopping'."
why_it_matters_hint: The White House and a leading AI company chief are publicly taking different positions on whether AI needs rules, just before the midterm elections.
event_date: Sunday 27 Sep and Monday 28 Sep 2026 (the article gives only the weekdays; those are the latest possible dates, since today is Saturday 3 Oct 2026)
notes: Local ABC7 page that carries an ABC News report; Google News shows it posted 3 Oct 2026, but the remarks are from the Sunday and Monday before. Dates are inferred from the weekdays in the article and are not printed in it. The article does not say Trump's Monday post is new policy. Altman's quotes are from his own social media posts as quoted by ABC.
